(Photo by Joe Buglewicz/Getty Images) (Joe Buglewicz/Getty Images) Geno Auriemma is back to having a manageable roster. After having an NCAA maximum of 15 scholarship players last year, UConn women's basketball has just 13 to start the 2026-27 season. It's the first time in four years that the Huskies have had fewer than 14 players. Auriemma, who begins his 42nd season, voiced his frustrations last year working with a maxed-out roster. The long bench not only made rotations difficult, but also made it hard to get everyone minutes. Auriemma works best with a small rotation. UConn lost five players in the offseason to either graduation or the transfer portal. Azzi Fudd (selected No. 1 overall by Dallas), Serah Williams (drafted No. 33 by the Connecticut Sun before getting traded to Portland) and Caroline Ducharme moved on to the professional stage. Ayanna Patterson (Kentucky) and Ice Brady (Florida State) left for other programs via the portal. In their place, Auriemma signed three newcomers, including two international stars and the nation's No. 2-ranked recruit. For the first time in three years, UConn didn't add any players through the transfer portal. Led by reigning National Player of the Year Sarah Strong and 2026 Big East Freshman and Sixth Woman of the Year Blanca Quiñonez, the Huskies may just have frontcourt depth for the first time in years. And seniors Ashlynn Shade and KK Arnold lead an eight-player guard room as Arnold begins her second year as UConn's primary point guard. The Huskies also shook up their coaching staff too - adding former UConn great Nykesha Sales as an assistant coach to replace fellow former Husky Jamelle Elliott, who left the staff in April after 18 years working alongside Auriemma and co. item.title: Odegaard urges Arsenal to bounce back after shock Fleetwood defeat: “We have a big game at the weekend”
item.description: Odegaard urges Arsenal to bounce back after shock Fleetwood defeat: “We have a big game at the weekend” Martin Odegaard has admitted Arsenal were 'not at our level' after they were knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Fleetwood Town. The Gunners' run in the competition ended in the fourth round, after a huge upset at Highbury Stadium. Fleetwood progressed on penalties after a 1-1 draw, in a fixture that saw 16-year-old Max Dowman sent off for the Gunners. Arsenal now have one fewer route to silverware this season, while the club's wait for League Cup success will extend into a 35th year. Odegaard did not hide from the performance when he gave his reaction to the club's official website after the defeat. Martin Odegaard: Arsenal 'not at our level' in Fleetwood cup exit "It's very frustrating to go out. Obviously, the way we’ve played was not on the level. We need to do much, much better than we did today. "Frustrating, but congratulations to Fleetwood and we look forward to the next game already and bounce back. "They did well so we have to give them credit, but I think today was about us not being on our level, we need to do better. I thought we improved during the game, but again, we need to step up even more - so that’s a shame. "We can't feel sorry for ourselves. We need to move on - we have a big game at the weekend [Liverpool], so bouncing back at the weekend is all we can do now."

item.title: China says takes Mbappe apology 'seriously' after Mao remark
item.description: Kylian Mbappe has been shut out of Chinese social media Weibo after he joked about Mao Zedong (Jade GAO) China said Wednesday it took "seriously" an apology from Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe after comments he made poking fun at Mao Zedong sparked a social media storm and saw Spanish football yanked off state TV. Mocking former leader Mao -- blamed by historians for millions of deaths -- is taboo in China and the French player's remarks saw him become the latest foreign sports figure to anger Beijing. In a clip of a video interview with French show The Bridge -- since taken down -- Mbappe talked about being amused by an internet meme of his face photoshopped onto "some guy, think he's a Chinese dictator", an apparent reference to Mao. "My comment was ill-judged and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world. I apologise to everyone my words have upset," the France captain said in a statement in French, Chinese and English on Tuesday. Foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing on Wednesday: "We take seriously the apology the individual concerned has made." La Liga, which saw the broadcast of its matches suspended in China, said it "deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappe's recent comments have caused among Chinese fans". But that may not be the end of the matter. Chinese beverage giant Dongpeng, which during this year's World Cup ran adverts with AI-generated images of Mbappe, said Tuesday it had scrapped its partnership with the player, as did dairy firms Mengniu and Milkground. CMG, which oversees public broadcaster CCTV, said it had decided to suspend broadcasts of the world's second-richest football league after England's Premier League. Mbappe's club also drew fire for not issuing any public apology, with "How much longer will arrogant Real Madrid keep playing ostrich" ranking fifth on search engine Baidu on Wednesday. Real "has neither criticised nor warned Mbappe over his conduct, let alone imposed any disciplinary measures", the state-run Global Times said in an editorial. Mbappe, 27, continued to face a torrent of criticism from Chinese web users on Wednesday, some of it racist. "His remarks were hurtful toward China and the Chinese people, so they cannot be translated," wrote one user on social media platform Weibo. Mbappe's original joke about Mao was not reposted -- or had been scrubbed -- from China's tightly controlled social media. Chinese social media app Xiaohongshu had meanwhile frozen Mbappe's account, where he has over a million followers. The same was done on the Weibo app, with a notice stating that "the user has been banned from following due to violating laws or the Weibo Community Convention". Some Chinese media reports said global brands like Dior and Hublot had removed their Mbappe-related content on Weibo. item.title: Can clubs stop team news leaking out through FPL picks?
item.description: Joao Pedro had been pictured in training before his shock absence from Chelsea's line-up last weekend [Getty Images] Chelsea head coach Xabi Alonso was caught off guard after Saturday's loss to Tottenham when asked whether he was aware that Joao Pedro's injury had been leaked through the popular Fantasy Premier League game. His response was: "I am not into the fantasy team thing, so I didn't know that." Accounts believed by FPL trackers to belong to Chelsea staff, a player and a relative of a player appeared to transfer out or bench Joao Pedro before the deadline. One Fantasy Premier League manager, known online as FPL Karim, was among those who believed they had identified information by tracking selections made by a relative of Chelsea forward Morgan Rogers. He said: "There were rumours that a player was missing from Chelsea's attack. I went to check Rogers' team, but he'd sold Joao Pedro two or three gameweeks earlier when he was injured. He never bought him back. "Then I checked his brother's FPL team and saw that he'd sold Joao Pedro that gameweek and brought in Nicolas Jackson. I thought it was a bit weird. Why would you sell him when he's one of the most-owned forwards in the game? "That's when I felt maybe it was Joao Pedro who was missing out. I posted about it, it went viral, and that was basically it." Confirmation of the injury emerged after the FPL deadline had passed, meaning 1.7 million managers had already selected Joao Pedro as captain, which doubles a player's points return. The absence also came as a surprise to many following Chelsea's 2-0 defeat by Tottenham, given Joao Pedro had been pictured in training during the week before the match. Alonso later said the striker had missed the game because of "fluid on his knee". 'Some players have started using aliases' Alonso is one of a number of managers who have become increasingly guarded when discussing team news in media conferences. Last month, he said: "I prefer not to give more information than needed." On that occasion, his side went on to lose 3-0 at Brentford, having kept several injury concerns, including one involving Joao Pedro, under wraps. Yet such is the popularity of Fantasy Premier League - a game played by more than 11 million people according to official figures - that many staff members, players and relatives of footballers also take part. By identifying leagues or teams linked to players, staff or family members through the game, which provides an open database of participants, it can be possible to infer what is happening behind closed doors at various training grounds. Previously, the highest-profile case involved Jack Grealish's absence from Aston Villa's match against Leicester City in February 2021. Leicester's manager at the time, Brendan Rodgers, admitted he had heard about the issue before the match, while Villa boss Dean Smith reportedly banned figures inside the club from playing FPL after the 2-1 defeat. item.title: £47m negotiations to begin for Liverpool to sign star
item.description: £47m negotiations to begin for Liverpool to sign star Ronald Araujo Liverpool Future Takes Shape as Permanent Transfer Talk Builds Liverpool’s early-season business already appears to have produced one of the more intriguing stories of the window, with Ronald Araujo making an immediate impression after arriving on loan from Barcelona. What initially looked like late-market cover is quickly being reframed as a potentially important piece of long-term planning under Andoni Iraola. According to Caught Offside , attention is now shifting towards whether Liverpool can convert that temporary move into a permanent deal. That change in tone has come swiftly, driven by the defender’s encouraging start and the sense that he has adapted well to Premier League demands. Barcelona and Liverpool Set for Ronald Araujo Decision The key detail centres on the structure of the agreement. There had been uncertainty over whether Liverpool held any route to buy, but the latest position is that a purchase option does exist and is set at €55m. If accurate, that gives Liverpool a clear reference point as they assess Araujo’s long-term suitability. Barcelona’s stance appears straightforward. The Spanish club were willing to sanction the loan, which speaks to their wider thinking around the player, but strong performances in England inevitably strengthen their hand. If Liverpool decide they want to keep him, negotiations are unlikely to be especially soft. Andoni Iraola Praise Highlights Strong Liverpool Start Araujo’s latest outing, in Liverpool’s 2-0 win over Brighton, only added to the growing sense that he may prove more than a short-term fix. Iraola’s post-match assessment underlined how highly the head coach has rated the defender’s opening contribution. Photo: IMAGO “It helps a lot [to have Ronald]. I think we all enjoyed watching Ronald fighting. I think he’s very good in the duels,” the Basque said. “Even the first goal, I think he wins two duels in a row, he arrives at the byline and after, it’s not an assist, but it’s worth an assist. And defensively, I think he’s been really, really really good.” Transfer Talks Could Accelerate Around €55m Option For Liverpool, the issue now is less about whether Araujo can cope and more about whether the club view €55m as value in the current market. If this level continues, that conversation will become increasingly serious. A defender with top-level pedigree, physical authority and visible early compatibility with Iraola’s demands tends to command significant fees. There is still distance between a promising loan and a completed permanent transfer, but Liverpool have given themselves a genuine opportunity. In a market where proven centre-backs are scarce and expensive, this may develop into one of the more sensible deals available to them. item.title: Liverpool already have the next Ballon d'Or winner
item.description: Liverpool already have the next Ballon d'Or winner Liverpool have already signed the next Ballon d'Or winner, and he's special. Everyone is celebrating Harry Kane at the moment. Rightfully so, he is the best player on the planet right now. Having been crowned with football's most prestigious award, Kane has put his name down in history. The award is well-deserved for the Bayern Munich forward. Kane has set incredible heights with his prolific goal-scoring over the course of the entire year. He has absolutely been instrumental in Bayern's success. Not to mention he performed very well at the World Cup as well leading England to another semi-final. There were other players who perhaps thought they might have been worthy of the title. Kylian Mbappe had another good season as usual, and Lamine Yamal was superb for Barcelona. But this year is Kane's and next year won't be Yamal's or Mbappe's either. The Ballon d'Or is changing and here's why For a long time, there was a hegemony in world football. Most of our generation were lucky to witness the supremacy of the Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi era. Everyone will have their personal opinion of who was the better player out of the two. However, objectively speaking there is no denying both were the two best players on the planet. No one even came close to their achievements. It felt at times as if they were superhuman. But things are different now. Ronaldo and Messi while still active players are no longer in their prime and the footballing landscape has shifted. The Ballon d'Or is changing as a result. It's now there for the taking. Players like Ousmane Dembele, Harry Kane and Rodri have proven it. Florian Wirtz will be the next Ballon d'Or winner Yes, you heard that right. We are backing the German to win it next year. Why? Because we are backing Andoni Iraola's side to go all the way both in the Premier League and the Champions League this season. With Man City's alleged charges looming in the air, the league is there for the taking. Meanwhile, Liverpool have already demonstrated they can be a huge threat in Europe. And the key to the Reds' success will be Wirtz. Liverpool signed him with high hopes and while he hasn't lived up to those hopes yet, he is starting to. His last four games have been brilliant and they have played a key role in catapulting Liverpool to success. If he maintains that kind of form, he will be performing at Bayer Leverkusen levels and if he does that and Liverpool win two major trophies - well then he's the obvious choice for the Ballon d'Or. That's why we are backing the next Ballon d'Or winner to be someone Liverpool have already signed. Wirtz, it's your time to shine.

item.title: Paul Merson calls out Mikel Arteta for scathing treatment of Max Dowman: ‘He’s a kid’
item.description: Paul Merson has called out Mikel Arteta for his scathing treatment of Max Dowman following the 16-year-old’s sending off against Fleetwood, claiming the Arsenal manager would not have done the same for more senior players. Dowman was shown a straight red card in the latter stages of Arsenal’s Carabao Cup humiliation against Fleetwood , which saw the League Two side dump out the Premier League champions on penalties after holding them to a 1-1 draw in 90 minutes. The teeanger was on the receiving end of a heavy challenge from behind from the Fleetwood midfielder Harrison Neal, who lunged at him near the touchline, and retaliated by kicking out to spark a brawl. After being given his marching orders by referee Michael Salisbury, there looked to be a furious reaction from Arteta towards Dowman as he walked off the pitch and went straight down the tunnel. Mikel Arteta had stern words for Max Dowman after his sending off (Getty) However, former Arsenal manager Merson believes Arteta was wrong to give Dowman such a public dressing down considering his age and early development. "You have to remember he is 16 years of age - he's a kid," he said on Sky Sports . "He wasn't having the greatest of nights so he's going to get frustrated. He gets the chance every now and then to play for Arsenal. "He probably feels he should be playing more. He gets the chance tonight, isn't doing too great. It's an old-fashioned tackle. "If that's Viktor Gyokeres , he [Arteta] isn't doing that. That's what I don't like. If it's an experienced international, I don't think he does that. He's a human being. "He's not the last person to get sent off for Arsenal and he's not the first." Fellow pundit Jobi McAnuff was similarly stunned at Arteta’s stern words for Dowman, who will now miss Arsenal’s next three games through suspension. "I'm really surprised,” he said. “Listen, maybe you know it's a bit of naivety, he's a young lad. But he [Arteta] gives him a proper talking to as he goes down the tunnel. "Clearly not happy with that ill-discipline. But we do have to remember he's a young boy - he's a kid - in a really high-pressure situation. Dowman was sent off for kicking out at a player against Fleetwood (Reuters) "I can't understand Mikel Arteta's reaction. Listen, he probably feels frustrated, he's the manager, he probably feels it's a bit petulant, a bit naive, which is what I think it is. "It's not really a full kick, his knee's kind of already in contact with the player, it's almost like a flick out really [after] the meaty challenge. It's frustration from Max Dowman after a bit of a difficult night. "But when we see the reaction from Mikel Arteta, we have to remember, this is a 16-year-old kid. Yes, he's got an Arsenal shirt on; yes, he's a fantastic talent. "He's going to make some mistakes along the way. I just felt the reaction, I didn't like it at all. He's obviously given him a little bit going down the tunnel."

item.title: Manchester United give Michael Carrick more time Despite poor run of results
item.description: Manchester United give Michael Carrick more time Despite poor run of results Manchester United have decided to give Michael Carrick more time to turn things around, according to The Athletic reporter Laurie Whitwell . The decision comes after an intense meeting between the club’s senior leaders on Monday. Carrick’s position as head coach was hanging by a thread following Sunday’s disappointing 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth at Old Trafford . They’re now 16th in the Premier League table after an eight-match winless streak. The loss was United’s second consecutive defeat by a three-goal margin, following their 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como on Wednesday. United have collected just seven points from their opening eight league matches, their worst start to a top-flight season in 40 years. However, co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox held discussions on Monday before deciding to keep Carrick in charge for now. He was at the club’s Carrington training ground on Monday to watch the Under-21s face Hull City, then returned to his usual duties on Tuesday. Carrick will lead the team against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday despite several difficult weeks at Old Trafford after a run of poor results. Captain Bruno Fernandes was left out of the starting line-up against Bournemouth for what Carrick described as “purely sporting reasons”. The Portuguese midfielder was an unused substitute in the 3-0 defeat after questioning Carrick’s tactics following the defeat to Como. Argentine centre-back Lisandro Martinez also criticised the club’s recruitment strategy in an emotional post-match interview a week earlier. Despite the poor results, United supporters still backed Carrick after Sunday’s defeat. Fans sang his name as he walked around the pitch to applaud them, before turning their anger towards the players. Carrick became United’s permanent head coach in May after impressing during his temporary spell in charge. He replaced Ruben Amorim in January and helped the club collect 39 points from their final 17 league matches, guiding them to third place.

item.title: La Liga reports 17 incidents from Barcelona vs Real Madrid Clasico including assault on Camavinga
item.description: La Liga reports 17 incidents from Barcelona vs Real Madrid Clasico including assault on Camavinga Real Madrid stormed back into the title race with a 2-1 victory over Barcelona at the Spotify Camp Nou . However, the game also witnessed several incidents involving supporters. The celebrations following Kylian Mbappe’s winning goal were particularly controversial. According to La Liga ‘s official report , also highlighted by El Partidazo de COPE , the competition has referred 17 incidents from Sunday’s Clasico to the Spanish Football Federation’s Disciplinary Committee and the Anti-Violence Commission. Barcelona supporters reported for chants and assault on Camavinga Of the 17 incidents documented, ten involved Barcelona supporters, including offensive chants directed towards Marc Cucurella, Jose Mourinho, Real Madrid and their fans. The report identifies two occasions when sections of the home crowd chanted “Cucurella, son of a b****” , while other supporters directed insults towards Mourinho and Madrid. More seriously, several Barcelona supporters threw bottles, cans, lighters and a vaping device towards the pitch during the celebrations following Mbappe’s second goal. Barcelona fans hurled abuse at Marc Cucurella during the game. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Although none of the objects struck Madrid’s players, the referee temporarily stopped the match for one minute and 20 seconds while a stadium announcement urged supporters to stop throwing objects. La Liga also confirmed that a spectator from Barcelona’s Grada Gol 1957 struck Eduardo Camavinga with a flag during the celebrations. Real Madrid supporters also mentioned in La Liga report Barcelona’s security staff subsequently identified the individual responsible for striking Camavinga, with the club preparing to expel the supporter under its internal regulations. Meanwhile, the remaining seven incidents involved travelling Real Madrid supporters, who repeatedly directed an offensive chant at Barcelona. Importantly, La Liga clarified that the incidents involving home supporters were concentrated in specific sections of the stadium, with the remaining Barcelona fans behaving appropriately. Camavinga was assaulted by Barcelona fans. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) For Madrid, the most concerning aspect remains the incident involving Camavinga. Players must be able to celebrate goals without facing physical aggression from spectators. Despite the intensity of the rivalry, attacking someone with a pole during a goal celebration is not warranted. The governing bodies will now assess the complaints and determine whether disciplinary sanctions are necessary. While Madrid can take satisfaction from their victory and the gap in La Liga being reduced to three points, these incidents do not make for great viewing, and it remains to be seen how the committees respond.

item.title: Mikel Arteta confirms fresh TRIPLE Arsenal injury nightmare as Declan Rice and two other stars face race to be fit for Liverpool clash after Fleetwood defeat
item.description: FBL-ENG-LCUP-FLEETWOOD-ARSENAL - AFP Arsenal have been hit by a devastating triple injury blow just as they prepare for a high-stakes Premier League showdown with Liverpool. Mikel Arteta has confirmed that several key first-team stars missed the club's midweek humiliating defeat to Fleetwood Town and are now facing a race against time to be fit for the weekend. Missing trio compounds Carabao Cup misery Arsenal suffered a humiliating penalty shootout elimination against League Two side Fleetwood Town on Tuesday night. Despite naming a strong starting line-up to navigate around his squad's growing fitness issues, Arteta was unable to call upon Declan Rice, Riccardo Calafiori, or Noni Madueke for the trip to Lancashire. Their sudden absence compounds a mounting availability crisis in north London. Arsenal are already navigating long-term injuries to key figures William Saliba, Bukayo Saka, and Christos Tzolis. Furthermore, Max Dowman will now serve a domestic suspension this weekend after receiving an ill-disciplined red card during the shock cup defeat, leaving the squad stretched incredibly thin. Arteta explains major fitness doubts Speaking after the unexpected early cup exit, the Gunners boss detailed the specific reasons behind his missing first-team regulars. He noted that Rice's issue originated during Saturday's 2-0 league victory over Everton, which ultimately forced an early substitution. "Calafiori was out, Noni was out with an ankle, and Declan was feeling a problem the other day (against Everton), which is why I had to substitute him," Arteta explained. Despite the frustrating defeat, the Spaniard refused to heavily criticise his depleted squad. Instead, he praised the fourth-tier hosts for pulling off a historic upset and commended the hostile environment they built on the night. "First of all, congratulations to Fleetwood," the Gunners boss said. "In the manner they did it, the atmosphere they created. I have nothing to fault the players for their attitude and intensity throughout the game, with 11 and with 10, but when you are playing in that superior way, you have to give nothing to the opponent." A 'very sad day' for wasteful Gunners Arsenal's shock defeat means their 34-year wait to lift the League Cup will stretch on for at least another season. Despite controlling the fixture, they crashed out before reaching the quarter-final stage, a result Arteta frankly described as a "very sad day" for the club as he highlighted their failure to convert dominance into goals. "When we create the volume of shots and chances we did, you have to score three, four or five," he said. "You capitalise on it. If you don't, there are no margins, and that's the reality. Then you have to wait and get through the round on penalties, and we didn't do that. That is very much what the 21-year-old has been doing - and more - since joining Liverpool in a deal worth £60m over the summer. Things could have been very different had Liverpool pressed further with their pursuit of Leny Yoro in 2024. Yet in going down that route, they were alerted to another French centre-back in Jacquet, who was playing for Rennes. Yoro chose to move to Manchester United from Lille and could well go on to be an elite centre-half but on Sunday afternoon, it was hard not to notice the difference between the pair. item.description: When Michael Wantz was hired as the Roncalli boys’ basketball coach in May of 2002, he kept hearing one thing over and over. “You need to get Pat to help you out.” Pat, Wantz soon learned, was Pat Crosley. He was a teacher in the school and had been helping previous coach Dave Gervasio prior to Wantz taking the job. But as Wantz quickly realized, labels like “teacher” and “coach” hardly summed up Crosley. “The most selfless servant leader,” Wantz said, his voice cracking when describing Crosley’s impact. “Sometimes it seems like hyperbole when you hear people talk about someone who just passed away. But Pat was that person. Everything you hear about Pat Crosley is true times ten. It’s a big loss for Roncalli. He literally died serving others.” Crosley, 58, died Friday while serving as a leader on the Roncalli Senior Christian Awakening Retreat at Camp Allendale in Trafalgar. He is survived by his wife of more than 30 years, Lori, adult daughters Molly and Betsy, both Roncalli graduates, his father Sherman, sister Traci Beck, and many other family members. He was preceded in death by his mother, Kathleen. Many of Crosley’s students at Roncalli, past and present, consider him family. After a brief stint at St. Jude Catholic School, he started out teaching religion at Roncalli, then transitioned into theology, history and U.S. government for almost 30 years at his alma mater. He worked more than 30 Christian Awakening Retreats for Roncalli seniors. In a podcast interview with Roncalli director of alumni and corporate relations Gary Armbruster in 2019, Crosley described the times when students would come back and tell him they enjoyed his classes. “Every once in a while it happens,” Crosley said. “And it’s validating, for sure. To hear kids say they liked my class … what did you learn? ‘I don’t remember.’ But they liked being in the classroom and that’s the kind of thing I’ve always wanted to be is a teacher, for better or worse, that you wanted to be in the room with.” Crosley, a 1987 Roncalli graduate, loved history. During a recent dinner with his longtime radio broadcast partner Rob Brown at Roncalli, he described how he would stop at cemeteries if they were on his route and look to see if any of the gravestones were from the Civil War era, then go home and try to research more about their lives. But there was more than one side to Crosley. “His friends all kind of joke that how does a guy with all of this intelligence and so many interests have Miller High Life as his favorite beer?” Brown said. “But that’s what he was. item.title: Huge Creative Changes Coming To WWE As Top Executive Set To RETIRE! (WWE News)
item.description: WWE Long-time WWE man Bruce Prichard is reportedly getting set to step away from the company. First reported by Mike Johnson over at PWInsider , Prichard is expected to retire from his position as Executive Director - Creative Writing & Talent (CWT) once WrestleMania 43 is done. Johnson notes that Bruce will remain "connected" to the company on a consultancy basis, but he would no longer retain his current duties and would no longer be based in Stamford, Connecticut. On this topic, Fightful Select adds that Bruce Prichard needs a "very serious" surgery, and that, post-WrestleMania 43, he'll still be doing work for WWE, but will be working from home. Fightful also points out that Prichard filled in for Triple H in running shows during the past few weeks while the Game was on vacation, and that an internal memo about Bruce's status was sent out earlier this year, though the details of that memo were not made public. Additionally, False Finish believes that situations such as the retirement of Bruce Prichard in a full-time role are something that will be happening "quite a bit" in the coming years, with WWE heading in a new direction and "currently contracted talent" expected to transition over to roles behind the scenes and in the office. The 63-year-old Prichard has been in the wrestling business dating all the way back to 1973, when he started selling posters for Paul Boesch's Houston Wrestling at just 10 years of age. The young Bruce would eventually start ring announcing and helping out with TV production for Boesch, and would also work for Bill Watts' UWF before landing in the then-WWF in 1987. By the summer of 1988, Prichard debuted his Brother Love character and The Brother Love Show, and would even be the Undertaker's first manager when the Phenom arrived at the 1990 Survivor Series. Bruce has had several spells with WWE over the decades, initially leaving shortly after that '91 Survivor Series, returning the following year and staying with the promotion until 2008, and then later returning in 2018 for the run he's currently on. In addition to working in various backstage roles for WWE, Prichard has also worked for the likes of TNA and MLW, and, of course, launched his hugely successful Something to Wrestle With podcast with Conrad Thompson - though commitments have meant that JBL has filled in alongside Conrad in recent times. item.title: Three things I want to see when Notre Dame plays Navy
item.description: SOUTH BEND, IN - OCTOBER 10: Notre Dame Fighting Irish WR Jerome Bettis Jr. (8) attempts to catch a pass during a college football game between the Stanford Cardinal and Notre Dame Fighting Irish on October 10, 2026 at Notre Dame Stadium in South Bend, IN. (Photo by James Black/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The No. 5 ranked Notre Dame Fighting Irish travel to New England to play the Navy Midshipmen for the 99th time in history. There isn’t a lot Notre Dame can do here to change any narrative for the better, and the SOS is going to take a hit — so they’re in a no win but gotta win big situation. So… what do I want to see? NO BS This is going to encompass a lot of different parts of the Notre Dame football team. I don’t want to see any kind of BS in this game. As good as CJ Carr is, I don’t want to spend half of the game watching him change plays, move guys around, check down, or anything else like that. It’s Navy… line up and go after them. I know that sounds a little crazy given how good CJ is at it, but it looks more like messing around against an opponent like Navy, and the Irish should be anything but a team that’s messing around after what happened in Provo. The defense isn’t immune to this point. There’s no reason Notre Dame’s defense shouldn’t manhandle the Navy offense. The last three meetings have been brutal for the Middies as they have only rushed for a combined 546 yards for a 186 average during the last three contests. This is a worse team than those three — so just go out there and dominate. CHANGES There was a different air around Marcus Freeman during the weekly presser, and as he talked about the BYU loss and Navy to come, he was asked a number of questions about doing things differently — like playing more than 3 wide receivers in a game. Say what you will about Freeman, but I do think he is quicker to pull the trigger on changes than a lot of coaches. I want to see some things “shook up” this week, and I don’t care about anyone’s feelings with this. It’s a week to stir up some shit — so stir it. STAY SAFE OUT THERE BOYS While there is a bad rap concerning Navy and the chop blocks against Notre Dame — this isn’t about that. Next week’s clash against the Miami Hurricanes will be the biggest regular season game at Notre Dame Stadium since the 2023 loss to Ohio State. The boys have to stay healthy. Say some prayers, eat the vitamins and protect your neck. I fully believe this season will be wilder than 2007 (which could be advantageous for the Irish) and I don’t fully believe that it will decide if Notre Dame is in the playoff or not — but it might be. Why leave it to chance? One of the best things the Irish can do to help themselves win that game, is by getting out of this game healthy. KEEP YOUR HEAD ON A SWIVEL BROTHER.

item.title: London Marathon considering major change to elite women’s race in 2027
item.description: The London Marathon could allow the elite women’s race in 2027 to unfold with male runners and pacemakers in pursuit of faster times and ultimately a world record. The overall world record, in mixed races, is held by Ruth Chepng’etich (2:09:56), though controversy surrounds that mark set at the 2024 Chicago Marathon after the Kenyan failed a drugs test five months later and was subsequently banned for three years in 2025. Tigst Assefa, who holds the women only race world record (2:15:41 from London Marathon 2026), appeared on track to break the overall world record at this year’s Berlin Marathon before rupturing her Achilles tendon in the closing stages and limping home in 2:11:04. Tigst Assefa ran with male pacemakers in Berlin, with London open to switching its format for 2027 (Getty) The distressing scenes left London Marathon CEO Hugh Brasher heartbroken for the Ethiopian athlete and now open to a change that could offer women, including Assefa, should she recover in time, a chance to better Chepng’etich’s controversial record in London next year. “Will London, in the future, have a women’s only record? Yes, I think that’s important,” Brasher, who is pushing for cleaner sport in the World Marathon Majors in light of Peres Jepchirchir’s provisional suspension after a failed test , told the Independent . “However, in the past, we’ve played around with it. Paula [Radcliffe], when she ran 2:15, had the women’s only record, so there were men running around her. She probably says they didn’t help her at all. “We’re prepared to mix it up. We very much talk to the athletes about what their goals are. I think what Tigst [Assefa] did in Berlin, it was a tragedy, in terms of the injury she got, we wish her well. It was incredible, she was going to beat that world record. It’s in touching distance. I’m sorry, but I think that world record is entirely dubious, if you study everything that’s been said, from the AIU, and what they believe, that’s a personal opinion.” The elite women’s race at London has been run as a women-only race in recent years, which usually poses a tougher challenge, given less depth of runners in and around the elite women’s time. However, Paula Radcliffe broke the women’s world record in mixed races (2:15:25) in 2003, with Brasher in discussions with the world’s best runners over which style of race they would prefer before an announcement on the elite fields expected in January. “We talk to the women and what they want to achieve, those conversation are still going on about 2027,” Brasher added. “We’re still signing athletes, and what we will have is some incredible racing, both men and women that are running, when we announce them in January, will have people salivating about racing. item.title: Pat Murphy Explains Why Brewers Didn’t Use Jacob Misiorowski
item.description: Jacob Misiorowski Brewers Pat Murphy Getty Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy explained why he didn’t use Jacob Misiorowski in Game 4 of the World Series. The Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays played an epic Game 4 on Tuesday night at Tropicana Field, with Tampa Bay eventually winning the game 4-3 in the 12th inning. Milwaukee carried a 3-2 lead into the bottom of the 12th inning, but ended up losing the game when the Rays came back against struggling Brewers reliever Shane Drohan, whose playoff ERA is now 18.00. Instead of using Drohan, though, Brewers fans were hoping that Murphy would use the team’s ace, Misiorowski, out of the bullpen. He chose to hold onto “The Miz,” and the Brewers blew the game. The Brewers still lead the Rays 3-1 in the best-of-seven World Series , with Game 5 taking place on Wednesday night in Tampa. So, why didn’t Murphy use Misiorowski? Pat Murphy Explains Not Using Jacob Misiorowski Speaking to reporters following the game, Murphy explained why he chose not to try to win Game 4 and the World Series with Misiorowski, the team’s best pitcher, entering in relief. Per Brewers reporter Curt Hogg , Murphy decided not to use Misiorowski in Game 4 because he was saving him for Game 5. “Pat Murphy said Jacob Misiorowski was not an option he wanted to burn in a one-run game in extra innings with a 3-0 series lead. item.title: Mikel Arteta remains tight-lipped on Max Dowman reaction after 16-year-old’s red card
item.description: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta refused to provide further explanation to his angry reaction to Max Dowman ’s red card in the Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood Town. But Arteta revealed what he said to Dowman as he walked off the pitch was to do with “something we discussed already before the match”. Arteta appeared to have harsh words for the the 16-year-old Arsenal forward following the first red card of his senior career, which came as the Gunners lost on penalties . Arteta appeared angered by Dowman’s red card (Getty) Dowman was making his second start of the season for Arsenal after his stunning two-goal display against Ipswich in the previous round of the competition. But Fleetwood made Arsenal’s night a frustrating one and the League Two side were hanging on for penalties when Dowman was sent off in the 85th minute. The teeanger was on the receiving end of a heavy challenge from behind from the Fleetwood midfielder Harrison Neal, who lunged at him near the touchline. Dowman kicked out at Neal in response to his tackle, sparking a brawl between the teams as the Fleetwood players reacted angrily to the youngster’s retaliation. The referee Michael Salisbury, who did not have VAR available, showed Dowman a straight red card for violent conduct, leaving Arsenal down to 10 men. And there looked to be an furious reaction from Arteta towards Dowman as he walked off the pitch and went straight down the tunnel. The incident took place on the opposite side of the pitch to Arteta’s dugout but the manager appeared to have sharp words for Dowman as he left the pitch. Dowman was sent off on his second start of the season (Reuters) Arteta said he still had to watch the incident back before commenting on it, but it was notable that he had no comforting words of support for the forward. “It’s difficult to see on the cameras like that so I’d prefer to watch it back properly so I can assess the situation,” he told Sky Sports. Asked if the 16-year-old can learn from the red card because of his young age, Arteta replied: “Yeah, we all learn from everything, yeah.” Then asked what he said to Dowman when he left the pitch, Arteta told BBC Radio 5 Live: “Something that we discussed already before the match.” Dowman will now be suspended for Arsenal’s next three Premier League games, starting with Sunday’s trip to Liverpool. It comes as Arteta is expected to be without his first-choice right winger, Bukayo Saka, due to injury for the next few weeks. And Arteta also revealed that his second-choice right winger Noni Madueke could be unavailable against Liverpool due to injury. It suggests Dowman could have been in line to start for Arsenal at Liverpool prior to his sending off at Fleetwood.

item.title: Lakers can’t get stops, suffer first loss of season
item.description: LOS ANGELES — The Lakers kept finding ways to score. Finding enough stops proved more difficult. Luka Doncic’s 41 points couldn’t prevent Los Angeles’ first loss of the season Tuesday night, dropping to 3-1 after a 136-129 loss to the Portland Trail Blazers at Crypto.com Arena. Portland had four players score more than 20 points. Ja Morant and Deni Avdija finished with 23 apiece, Jrue Holiday added 22 off the bench and Damian Lillard scored 21, including a sidestep 3-pointer with 43 seconds remaining that iced the game and push their undefeated record alive to 3-0. Their balanced production, combined with fouls and defensive breakdowns, kept the Lakers from sustaining momentum. “We got broken down a lot,” Lakers coach JJ Redick said. “The game plan discipline, KYP personnel discipline wasn’t where it needs to be.” Austin Reaves contributed 26 points and seven assists, and Sandro Mamukelashvili added 17 points for L.A. The Lakers committed 16 first-half fouls, giving the Trail Blazers 21 free-throw attempts before halftime. L.A. ended the night with 29 fouls that gave Portland 41 attempts (made 26) at the free throw line. Flopping calls added to the interruptions, disrupting the Lakers’ rhythm as they tried to build on an efficient offensive start. L.A. shot better than 56% from the field, but Portland shot 59% and made 18 of 36 3-point attempts. “If we score 129 points at home, we should be able to get enough stops to win,” Redick said. The Lakers opened by making five of their first six shots for a 14-7 lead. Doncic scored 16 first-quarter points, including two 3-pointers, helping L.A. take a 38-32 advantage. Portland stayed close by making 10 of 14 shots in the period, then opened the second quarter with a 26-16 run. As the Lakers’ foul total climbed, the Trail Blazers repeatedly reached the line, preventing L.A. from establishing a sustained run. Mamukelashvili provided a lift with a buzzer-beating 3-pointer that sent the Lakers into halftime ahead 73-68. Doncic had 24 points, while Reaves added 14 points, five rebounds and four assists. Portland changed the momentum and erased any Lakers lead or momentum in the second half, outscoring the L.A. 68-56. “We still have to be mindful of turnovers,” Reaves said. “But yeah, offense has been good.” Portland’s fourth-quarter zone presented another challenge. Redick said the Lakers generated open shots, but they couldn’t consistently follow those possessions with stops. L.A. cut the deficit to 114-112 as defensive chants grew louder. item.description: Arteta insists attitude not to blame as Arsenal exit Carabao Cup to Fleetwood Mikel Arteta has insisted he "cannot fault" the attitude of his Arsenal players after a Carabao Cup fourth-round defeat on penalties to Fleetwood Town. The League Two side, who sit 18th in the fourth tier, knocked out last season's finalists after a shoot-out on Tuesday night. Fleetwood arrived as specialists from the spot. According to Opta , they have now won their last four penalty shoot-outs in all competitions, converting each of their last 16 spot-kicks across those shoot-outs. Before the game, Arteta had warned that Arsenal could not drop their standards if they were to avoid an upset, but saw his side crash out of the competition in a huge upset. Speaking after the final whistle, Arteta congratulated the hosts and defended his squad's effort. "Congrats to Fleetwood, it's a sad day for us. But I cannot fault at all the attitude of the players. "Max Dowman's red card? I prefer to watch it back properly, and then I can assess the situation. We learn from everything." So what are their chances of beating Chelsea? Chelsea confirm major injury ahead of Liverpool clash Chelsea head coach Xabi Alonso has confirmed that Joao Pedro will not face Liverpool at Anfield. It's an enormous blow for the Blues, who have come to depend on the Brazilian in all truth. Pedro has started the season superbly and his link-up play with Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer behind him has been the primary reason for any Chelsea success this season. They'll be without him again, though, much as they were in the 2-0 defeat at home to Spurs this weekend.
